newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico City fuel blast injures at least 11.
newsitem.headline: Mexico City fuel blast injures at least 11.

text.p: At least 11 people were injured on Monday when a fuel storage tank owned by state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) exploded in a suburb of Mexico City, officials said.

A dense cloud of thick, black smoke rose thousands of feet (metres) into the air from the site of the explosion and was visible from virtually all points of the capital as the fire spread to a second tank and raged for hours. The smell of burnt gasoline hung in the air.

A man claiming to be a Mexican Red Cross commander told local radio four people had died in the blast and more than 900 had suffered smoke inhalation, but Red Cross officials contacted by Reuters said they did not know who he was.
"We heard a loud noise, we didn't know what it was. Then we saw the fire," said a shaken Lourdes Rivas Mendoza, a 30-year-old housewife who lives a few blocks from the site of the blast.
The blast was caused when gasoline leaked from a faulty valve on one of the storage tanks, Pemex administrative director Humberto Lira Mora told a news conference.

He said the storage tank contained at least 80,000 barrels of gasoline -- equivalent to about 4.7 million litres (1.25 million gallons). A second tank containing 25,000 barrels of fuel also caught fire, he said.
The blaze was contained but would not burn out until sometime Tuesday, he said.
Hundreds of firemen battled the blaze while hundreds more police and dozens of army troops evacuated nearby residents from their homes and kept curious onlookers away from the blaze's intense heat.

Mexico City mayor Oscar Espinosa Villareal and Lira both said 11 people were injured in the blast and none were dead. Doctors in area hospitals said most victims suffered second- and third-degree burns.
Bloodied firemen were seen being taken on stretchers to hospitals, their faces raw with burns and swathed in bandages.
"We have been able to evacuate several families and no one else is in danger," Espinoza said after visiting the site.
Television network TV Azteca reported that a firefighter had died but his father, choking back tears, later told reporters his son, although badly burned, was alive.
The explosion occurred at 3:05 p.m. (2105 GMT) at Pemex's storage and distribution centre in the industrial suburb of San Juan Ixhuatepec.
TV Azteca said lcal residents had been pressing for some time for the depot to be relocated because of safety concerns.
The San Juan district was the site of a huge gas explosion 12 years ago which killed hundreds of people.

The explosion was the second in recent months at a Pemex installation. On July 26 a blast caused by human error at the firm's Cactus gas processing centre in the southern state of Chiapas killed six workers.
In April 1992, an explosion in Mexico's second-biggest city, Guadalajara, killed more than 200 people after gasoline leaked from a Pemex pipeline into the sewer system.
